en: Wow, I can't believe it was that close! That really got my blood pumping good!
That was a lot of fun! I need to head back home now, though. <Color:255,200,200,255>⑮<Color:Default>
That was a lot of fun! Please give me a call again sometime! <Color:255,200,200,255>⑮<Color:Default>
Oh, I win! I knew I wouldn't lose to you, Shinada-san.
How remarkable that we managed to have a draw! I'll be sure to win next time, though!
That was quite fun! I'll be heading back to Nagoya now. <Color:255,200,200,255>⑮<Color:Default>
That was such fun! Please do call me again! <Color:255,200,200,255>⑮<Color:Default>
You're really good at that, Kiryu-san! I'm kinda surprised!
Yay, I win! Looks like you have to practice some more, Kiryu-san!
Wow, I can't believe it was a tie! But I'm gonna win next time!
That was super fun! Ask me out again sometime! <Color:255,200,200,255>⑮<Color:Default>
That was fun! I'm here to take you on anytime you want! See ya!
Welcome! How would you like to play today?
Not right now, sorry.
No, not right now.
Nah, not now.
No, not now.
Sorry, but I can't.
I see. Please come again anytime.
I'll be playing by myself.
I'll play solo.
It'll just be me playin'.
Is it cool if I play alone?
I'll be playing alone.
Very well. That'll be 500 yen, please.
Okay, sure.
This okay?
Ah, sure, sure.
Sure, all right.
Three frames.
Ten frames.
(I ain't got the money.)
You can play against me.
I'll play against you.
You and me, let's do this.
Can I have a game against you?
Can I play against you?
That'll be 500 yen.
Sure, please.
Then let's begin.
I'll play a split game, please.
I'll have a split game, please.
I'll do a split game.
Is it cool if I play a split game?
I see. That'll be 500 yen, please.
Y'gotta be kiddin' me! Y'called me all the way out to Tokyo jus' to go bowling!?
Well, you can do some sightseeing before you head back, too. Shall we get started?
It'll be 1,000 yen for two players. How many frames would you like to play?
Sorry to keep y'waiting! You wanted to go bowlin' with me, Kiryu-san?
Ready to get started?
It'll be 1,000 yen for the two of you. How many frames would you like to play?
Going into work is enough of a pain as it is, but you go and call me all the way out here to Tokyo!? Unbelievable!
Sorry for the wait! It's good to get out every once in a while! <Color:255,200,200,255>⑮<Color:Default>
Wanna get started?
Ya called up a student who's busy lookin' for a job all the way out in Osaka, just to go bowlin'? If this is a joke, I ain't laughin'.
Sorry for makin' ya wait! You're really up for anything, aren't ya, Akiyama-san? <Color:255,200,200,255>⑮<Color:Default>
Apologies for the delay! I'm rather nervous. It's been quite a while since I last bowled.
(I'll give Hinata a call.)
Sorry for the wait! And wow, I almost never go bowling with just two people!  <Color:255,200,200,255>⑮<Color:Default>
Want to get started?
(I'll give Hinata-chan a call.)
It's all right. Shall we begin?
(I should give Mach-ko a call.)
(I'll give that Mach-ko a call.)
(Guess I'll give that Mach-ko a call.)
(I should call up that Mach-ko gal.)
(Maybe I should call that Mach-ko-san person.)
Hehe! Sorry to keep you waiting! There are no words necessary between bowling aficionados. Just bring your A game!
You going to fish here? Y'know what, I bet you are. You look like quite the fisherman, I just know it!
No, I...
Huh? Me?
By the way, if you don't have any bait, I'll sell you some. I always come here with a veritable mountain of bait, I do.
See, I love fishing, but I'm not the best fisherman. Never catch anything myself. So, if you ever have too many fish, I'll buy 'em off you. Good deal, huh?
Oh, and that fishing rod there is mine, but you're more'n welcome to use it. I'm going to take me a quick break.
Hey, you a fishing enthusiast too? Let me know if there's any way I can help you. I got me a soft spot for new and aspiring fishermen.
Alrighty then, what would you like?
Thanks. Say the word if you need more.
Alrighty then, what do you got for me?
Thank you. Take care now.
Is that so? Well, you come by again whenever you're in the fishin' mood.
(I can't afford the fare. Better scrounge up 710 yen...)
The base fare is 710 yen. Where are you headed?
Sorry, I have urgent business back in Sotenbori.
No problem. I'll be waiting here, so let me know when you get back.
Would you like to go back to Kamurocho?
Ah, Shinada. Hm? You're with a friend. We'll leave any talk of training for another day.
Coach Igarashi.
Oh, right, Shinada. I found another good online shop. Here, I'll show you.

You learned about Import.net!
...Time to get clicking!
There's nothing left for me to teach you.
I've given you all the training you'll need. And I must say, you've grown quite admirably.
Now go on and settle things from your past.
I see you finally put your past to rest, huh? Well done.
But the road to better batting continues without end. Stay the course, kid.
Coach, I did it. I caught a marlin.
Ah, well done. Your dynamic visual acuity should've improved significantly.
Specifically, your ability to concentrate on pitches will have improved⑬the length of time the ball appears stationary will be longer.

I sure hope so. That was one slippery challenge, and not the
kind I'm used to!

You've reached a new breakthrough in batting potential!
Your Heat Eye was enhanced.
So this is it for training, huh?
Yes. You know, I'm really impressed that you stuck with it to the end. You are my best student, after all.
Nah... I just did as I was told. You're the one who decided to train me, Coach.
Heh. You're about the only student who has that sort of attitude.
Aw shucks...
You see, I retired because no one was listening to me anymore.
Scientific training methods are all the rage these days. People called my ways outdated and gave up on me.
But you know, seeing your incredible growth, I'm convinced my style wasn't wrong. I feel confident as a trainer again.
Then, does that mean what I think it means?
Yes. I think I'm going to resume coaching. My retirement's canceled.
You're too young to be going out to pasture anyway.
I'll stay in Nagoya a while longer, though. I want to see how things turn out for you.
Cool.
Go to Nagoya Wharf and catch a marlin. A marlin has power and endurance like you wouldn't believe, so it'll take everything you got to land one.
Here I am for training, Coach.
Good, let's get to it. What were we going to do? Improve your dynamic visual acuity?
Yes. Something about getting nutrition and building a foundation.
That's right. By getting the nutrition one needs, the benefits of training become more pronounced.
As such, proper nutrition is essential to improving dynamic visual acuity.
Okay. So what should I do?

Hold your horses. You should know, this will be your final
training session.
Huh? This is it?
That's right. This last training will bring your batting skills up to where they need to be.
After that, there's nothing more for me to teach.
I see... Well, what's this final training you have for me?
Go sea fishing. Nagoya's wharf will do.
Sea fishing!? Nope, never mind⑬I've decided nothing surprises me anymore. Why that, though?
To get you to focus. When sea fishing, concentrating on the movements of your catch is absolutely paramount, lest your line be broken.
The fish are also more powerful. Some of them you'll have to battle for quite a while before you can finally reel them in.
Yeesh. Sounds intense.
As it should be. You need stamina to win a battle of endurance. That's why I've been telling you to get the fundamental nutrients you need.
Okay... I'm sorta convinced?
See? I've thought your training through.
All right then, Coach. Off to the rough and stormy waters I go.
Hold on, hold on. You need to catch a marlin. Understood?
...Does it have to be a marlin?
Of course. Did you think you could just snag a goby and be done with it?
A marlin is the pinnacle of piscine power and endurance. It will take your all to land one.
Got it. Then I'm gonna reel me in the biggest marlin you ever saw!
I'm back, Coach.
Ah, Shinada. Did you go eat some chicken dishes?
Sure did. I ate chicken at at least three restaurants, just like you said.
Good. Your dynamic visual acuity should be better. You'll be able to see the ball in motion with better clarity.
I sure hope so. Gotta test it out next time.
Oh, and if I want to keep improving my vision, I should keep eating more chicken?
No, I'm afraid it doesn't work that way.
...Knew it.
Consider this akin to laying down the foundation of a building. The nutrients found in chicken are the basis for further growth in your abilities.
Next time, I'll teach you that training method.
Today, chicken's on the menu. Eat it at three different places in Kineicho, minimum. And three things at the same restaurant won't count. That'd just be dishonest.
I'm here, Coach! Train me up right!
Oh, you're back again. All right, let's not waste any time. I'll have you hone your dynamic visual acuity even further.
Oh, like the time you made me eat anthocyanins? What should I do this time?
Hit the town and go scarf down some chicken.
Chicken? So I should be eating more protein now?
That's right. Chicken is ideal for its ample amount of animal protein. Plus, Nagoya's famous for the stuff.
You get to eat well, and you gain the benefits of training. Isn't that a win-win situation?
It would be... if I didn't have to pay for it.
Did I mention you have to try at least three different restaurants? You can't just go to one place and expect to learn everything.
Aww, why not?
Every restaurant prepares and flavors their food differently. Nutritional intake varies with the cooking method, temperature, added ingredients, and so on.
This training also makes you locate good restaurants. That alone should improve your attention and mental strength.
You really think so? Well, I'm not one to argue.  Then I'm off to find the tastiest chicken in town!
You do that. Get some good nutrition into you.
Ah, yes. Well? Did you manage to eat food with anthocyanins?
I did. It certainly was a challenge, but I managed somehow.
Good. That should have improved your dynamic visual acuity.
Remember your ability to focus and see pitches as if they were suspended in time? That ability should be more pronounced now.
Oh, that thing. Yeah, I'll definitely give that a try.
I'll go eat some more anthocyanins, too. That's gonna keep improving my vision, right?
I highly doubt that.
...Why?
Training isn't that simple. This time, your dynamic visual acuity was improved using a certain form of nutrition, but don't expect that to happen every time.
Anyhow. If you want to enhance this ability further, come see me again.
Go out and find food that contains anthocyanins. There should be plenty in town.  Simple enough for you?
Hey, Coach. What you got for me today?
Ah, Shinada. Here to train? Then I'd be glad to help you.
Let's see now... How about working on your dynamic visual acuity?
Oh, was that the one where you made me go fishing? Okay, I'll go grab some worms off the ground and⑬
Don't get ahead of yourself. It's not fishing this time.
...Then what is it?
You should like this. We're taking a nutritional approach this time.
Nutritional? As in, I should eat something?
That's right. By giving your body the nutrition it needs, the benefits of training become more pronounced.
I can dig it. Hey, isn't there some nutrient that's good for the eyes or whatever?
Indeed there is. It's called anthocyanin. Now go eat something that contains it.
That's it? Psh, that doesn't sound too hard.
Of course not. All you're doing is eating. There's no challenge whatsoever, unless you've stuffed yourself beforehand or something.

Heheh, this one's in the bag. So what kind of food contains
anthocyanins?
No idea.
...Come again?
I said I have no idea. You go find it yourself, whatever has anthocyanins in it.
Coach, have I ever told you you're a hardass?
Shut your whine-hole and get on with it.
Dammit. Fine, I'll get out there...
Ah, you're back. Did you get your prize?
Yup. Got the dragon, as instructed.
Good job. So, how was it? Do you feel like you can foul off pitches better?
I haven't noticed that yet, no. But, I do feel like I've gotten into the habit of seeing better in three-dimensional space.
